title: Banks Face $500 Billion In Losses: Debt Bomb Strikes | Chris Whalen
speaker: Chris Whalen

macro_themes.view: Industry sits on ~$500B of securities losses; an earnings problem, not a solvency one, worst at Bank of America and Schwab.
Inflation and the Iran war will push bank credit costs up; he is out of banks and short a couple of names.
Bonds may rally but 10s won't go back to 5% or lower; Treasury/White House statements have eroded confidence.
AI is a mania funded by circular finance; Oracle, CoreWeave and others likely end up restructured or bought.
Continuation vehicles signal unsellable assets; PE is a train wreck.
Shift to a buyer's market, mortgage volumes falling to ~$1.7-1.8T next year; rental-property business-purpose loans will be a problem next year.
Energy stays elevated and food prices rise into spring due to fertilizer (sulfur) shortages; core is okay.
US is sleepwalking into a debt crisis that ends with Fed buying securities and inflation.

calls.instrument_quoted: bank stocks generally (no specific names given)
calls.reason: Credit costs will rise due to inflation and the Iran war; Wall Street capital-markets revenue slowing and loan growth weak.
calls.quote: I'm out of banks... I'm actually short a couple names right now because I think credit costs... are going to go up.

calls.reason: Fed not buying securities, eroded confidence in US policy and AI credit demand keep yields high; a bond rally may come but limited.
calls.quote: we may see a rally in bonds, but are we going to go back to 5% on the on 10s uh or lower? I don't think so.

calls.reason: Debt commitments its balance sheet can't handle, force majeure notices on data-center deals lacking power; near junk status.
calls.quote: you almost know that they're going to end up in trouble. I think Oracle is a case in point.

calls.reason: Builders must move unsold inventory (subsidies, rentals) and face cost pressure forcing smaller homes and fewer spec builds.
calls.quote: Would you be a buyer of home builders now...? No. No, not at this level.

notes: Bank short is unnamed names; KBE used as sector proxy. Homebuilder ETF is described as State Street's (XHB assumed). Mortgage rates ~7.4-7.6%, 10y 5.1% quoted by host. Bearish on BAC/SCHW management but framed as earnings issue, not a trade call; CoreWeave mentioned with Oracle but not a separate call.
